objective_strength.title: Current, treatment-specific Social proof gives prospective patients useful decision context.

binding_constraint.title: Reputation does not accumulate or respond to enough recent treatment evidence.
binding_constraint.statement: Reputation does not accumulate or respond to enough recent treatment evidence. Prospective patients who reach the clinic see weaker current proof than the fictional comparison set, so trust stalls before enquiry.

top_priorities.title: Create a neutral, universal review-request workflow.
top_priorities.impact: A consistent invitation to every eligible patient can address low velocity without selective routing.
top_priorities.why_now: The practice presents less current patient evidence than every named comparator in the same 90-day window.
top_priorities.expected_effect: A neutral invitation to every eligible patient can address low velocity without selective routing; it does not guarantee review volume.

top_priorities.title: Respond consistently and privacy-safely.
top_priorities.impact: Broader and faster acknowledgement would make the reputation surface visibly active.
top_priorities.why_now: Most synthetic reviews receive no timely acknowledgement, so the surface looks inactive.
top_priorities.expected_effect: Broader, privacy-safe responses would make reputation look attended; coverage is not a rating or patient forecast.

top_priorities.title: Use recurring treatment themes to improve operations and proof continuity.
top_priorities.impact: Better decision detail can reveal operational themes and connect real feedback to other surfaces.
top_priorities.why_now: Reviews rarely name treatments or clinicians, so decision proof stays on Social only.
top_priorities.expected_effect: Theme work can improve operations and proof continuity without scripting sentiment or promising review depth.

do_not_do.title: Do not use incentives, sentiment filtering, selective routing, or any form of review gating.
do_not_do.rationale: Funding new acquisition before reputation is repaired would send more patients into a trust leak: low 90-day velocity and missing responses make the practice look less current than named peers. Incentives or gating would also distort the same evidence.
revisit_after: A neutral invitation workflow covers every eligible patient
Response coverage is visibly active on the current review sample

remediation_tasks.outcome: Every eligible patient receives the same neutral review invitation through a documented, platform-compliant workflow.
steps: Define the same objective eligibility event for every patient without using sentiment, rating or complaint status.
Choose the permitted invitation channel and write neutral copy that allows any honest feedback.
Configure one universal trigger, suppression rule for duplicate sends and an operational owner.
Audit a disclosed sample for invitation coverage and retain the workflow evidence.
prerequisites_access: Practice messaging-system access for the chosen implementer

sequence.rationale: A neutral invitation process addresses the measured recency and velocity gap without prohibited selection.

remediation_tasks.owner_role: Practice operations lead with privacy/compliance acceptance
remediation_tasks.effort_complexity: Medium — copy is simple, but trigger design, platform rules and unbiased coverage require careful operations work.
remediation_tasks.implementation_risk: Sentiment filtering, incentives or selective routing can become prohibited review gating; use one neutral rule for every eligible patient.
remediation_tasks.horizon: Workflow setup within one to two weeks; review recency develops over a longer window without a volume guarantee.
remediation_tasks.next_action: Approve one objective eligibility event that applies equally to every patient.

remediation_tasks.outcome: Eligible reviews receive timely, privacy-safe acknowledgement under one owned response standard.
steps: Define the response owner, daily review check and escalation path for sensitive or negative content.
Create short response patterns that acknowledge feedback without confirming treatment or patient status.
Backfill only the selected recent sample, starting with unresolved negative reviews under privacy review.
Measure response coverage and observable response delay over the next disclosed sample window.
prerequisites_access: GBP response access for the chosen responder

sequence.rationale: Response ownership follows the invitation standard so one operator can manage both current-review workflows consistently.

remediation_tasks.owner_role: Trained reputation responder with practice/privacy escalation support
remediation_tasks.effort_complexity: Medium and ongoing — initial standards are bounded, while daily coverage creates continuing operating load.
remediation_tasks.implementation_risk: A response can expose protected or clinical information or become argumentative; prohibit confirmation of patient status and escalate sensitive cases.
remediation_tasks.horizon: Initial standard in days; coverage and speed should be assessed over at least one documented review window.
remediation_tasks.next_action: Name the daily response owner and privacy escalation reviewer.

remediation_tasks.outcome: Recurring public feedback themes inform operations and are reflected across surfaces without scripting, prompting for positive sentiment or copying patient claims.
steps: Code a disclosed review sample by treatment, clinician, process and experience themes without identifying patients.
Separate operational gaps from reusable public proof and send sensitive themes to the internal owner only.
Use aggregate, truthful themes to improve treatment-page questions and clinician education content.
Recheck review depth and Cross-Surface proof continuity using the same rubric.

sequence.rationale: Theme work follows the neutral invitation and response standards so proof continuity never drives selective collection.

remediation_tasks.owner_role: Research/content strategist with operations and clinical/compliance acceptance
remediation_tasks.effort_complexity: Medium to high — requires consistent coding, privacy review and coordinated content changes across more than one surface.
remediation_tasks.implementation_risk: Cherry-picking positive comments or reproducing identifiable claims would distort evidence; use disclosed samples and aggregate themes only.
remediation_tasks.horizon: Initial theme set in two to four weeks; deeper public evidence matures over multiple review cycles.
acceptance_evidence: De-identified theme ledger with disclosed sample
Live aggregate-theme content and repeat rubric check
remediation_tasks.next_action: Select the first dated review sample and approve the de-identification rules.

roadmap_preview.disclaimer: Illustrative sequencing based on this diagnosis. Final Sprint scope is confirmed separately.

implementation_paths.diy: Assign an operations owner, trained responder and content reviewer; follow tasks 1–3 without incentives, sentiment filtering or selective routing.
implementation_paths.other_provider: Give another reputation provider the complete task plan and insist on universal eligibility, privacy-safe responses, disclosed samples and the listed acceptance evidence.
implementation_paths.defer: Keep the 90-day baseline and monitor response coverage, but do not substitute paid reputation tactics or a gated review funnel for the diagnosed workflow.
implementation_paths.caesthetic: Ask CAESTHETIC to scope selected workflow, response and theme tasks with explicit platform/privacy controls in a separate Sprint statement.

why_caesthetic.evidence_advantage: CAESTHETIC has already connected the synthetic 90-day comparison, response pattern and Cross-Surface proof gap into one evidence ledger.
why_caesthetic.coordination_advantage: The workload crosses operations, platform configuration, daily response ownership, privacy escalation and content acceptance; coordinated execution can reduce handoff risk without hiding any step.
why_caesthetic.sprint_boundary: The Score does not pre-sell a review campaign or promise review volume. A 30-Day Sprint confirms selected work, access and acceptance evidence separately and cannot guarantee ratings, patients or revenue.
why_caesthetic.ownership: The practice owns and may reuse the report, evidence and full task plan with its own team or any provider. There is no exclusive method or lock-in.

methodology.competitorSelection: Three named fictional aesthetics clinics selected by synthetic market proximity and treatment overlap.
methodology.limitations: All practices, people, observations, competitors and scores are synthetic. The safe review-system diagnosis does not use incentives, filtering, selective routing or review gating. No outcome is guaranteed.
